title: Shiva cuts Brahma's head (Kapali / Kashi) and Narada's Maya
key_part2: G (from 316.08 s, Narada / Maya / Vishnu half)
bpm_range: 48-72 slow dread and sorrow; 84-108 build; 132-168 chase; 104 playful part 2; 150 flood
anchor_convention: t = absolute seconds from voice_timeline.md. 'word' = the spoken word at that time (punctuation as in the timeline). If 'edge':'end' is present, t is the END of that line (line end time from the timeline header) and word is the last word of that line. 'silence' cues are MUSIC drop-outs only (the voice is never cut); most are 0.35-1.0 s and sit in word gaps or the listed pauses.

shraap.note: MAIN THEME of the episode, the curse: root, flat 2nd, flat 3rd, back to root (E F G E), a tight chromatic turn that cannot escape itself. Low horn doubled by cello. First heard on 'श्राप।' (17.92), full on 'बेटे' (21.80), returns slower at 37.94, on 'शब्द हार गए' (108.82), on 'ब्रह्महत्या।' (200.82) in the lowest register, and in the teaser at 486.98 'श्राप' to promise the next story.

brahma.note: Creator: slow, grand, sustained, a wide rising fifth settling on the 5th. Corrupted version (flat 6th held, tremolo strings, trombone) when his gaze changes (61.98, 65.46, 117.22); hollow, low organ at 191.40; pure and gentle again at 159.70 (regret), 177.86 (four faces) and 218.24 (Atri).

brahmi_fear.note: Brahmi's flight and fear: a falling line that never lifts. Innocent version (31.14, 54.36) is flute and harp with a raised 3rd. Violins, fast (69.10, 114.44). Solo cello alone in her speech (279.32 to 290.36). Climbs a step with each 'उन्हें X देने से' line and breaks open on the last line (314.00 to 316.02).

shiva_wrath.note: Fury and justice: stern fourth, then back down to the root, over a damaru roll and taiko. Entrance 152.80 'शिव', resumes 164.70 as the anger refuses to cool, mellow and weary as 'महादेव' at 222.98.

kapali.note: The wandering penitent: slow, heavy, a step down to the leading note below the root, never quite arriving. Over wind and slow footsteps. Named at 247.14 'कपाली।'.

kashi.note: Release and grace: the Kapali line turned upward into Yaman light. Hint 258.58, bansuri 265.58, full shehnai + choir + conch on 'काशी।' (270.98).

narada.note: Playful, bright, always on the move: a quick rising run that ends on the 5th (a question). Slow dorian veena in part 1 when he cursed (36.44), wistful at 438.24, left open at 470.82.

maya.note: Illusion: shimmering santoor with the flat 2nd and sharp 4th, never resolving; a detuned pad underneath. Glimpse 337.58, full 349.34 (the maiden), 418.26 (the reveal), returns unresolved at 472.64 and 479.32.

vishnu.note: Calm, luminous, a cradle shape that rises and gently returns. Tanpura on Sa-Pa is the constant of every Vaikuntha moment.

series_logo.note: Series signature at the very end (491.66 + 3 s tail). Start-of-episode logo is not placed (voice begins at 0.14 s), see requests.

cues.note: Cosmic hum with a thin cold wind: a god wandering the universe with the skull. Very low.
Low E drone below 200 Hz from the first word: hook is dark from the first second.
Short reverse swell that climbs 'एक देवता ने दूसरे देवता का सिर...' straight into the cut.
HOOK HIT: one taiko crack plus sub boom on 'काट' (head cut). Sub under 120 Hz and crack above 5 kHz, nothing in the voice pocket.
Slow heartbeat starts when the severed head clings: dread with a pulse.
Dry bone knock and a sticky crackle: the skull sticks to the hand.
Whispering tremolo (E / F) for 'no mantra, no penance': helplessness.
One distant, slightly cracked temple bell: prayer that did not work.
Wide air-shimmer: the whole cosmos.
Low brass and string riser through 'जड़ में है एक...' to the word 'श्राप।'.
Brass braam on E-F cluster plus sub boom: the curse arrives.
SHRAAP (main theme), statement 1 in the lowest horn register.
BRAHMA motif hint on his name, low organ.
Short music drop-out one beat before the twist word 'बेटे' (his own son). Only the E drone stays, very low.
TWIST HIT: timpani + sub + choir stab. 'His own son cursed him' is the hook's last punch. Tail runs out through 'दिया था।'.
SHRAAP full statement (horn + cello + brass) under the reveal.
Creator's world: grand, warm, slow organ and choir pad. The contrabass drone continues quietly.
BRAHMA motif, full, on 'रचयिता' (the Creator).
Harp sparkle for the two creations.
Soft tinkle-bell on 'मनु'.
BRAHMI innocent form: flute with the 3rd raised, sweet. The same falling shape will return as fear.
Warm swell: the first couple on earth.
'पर इसी बीच': warmth cooled into tremolo, an E / F minor-2nd shiver.
NARADA motif, slow and dark dorian veena (the curse-giver).
SHRAAP, statement 2, slower, with a quiet brass cluster underneath.
Whispered choir oohs for the curse's words (the quote).
Glass shimmer reversed: forbidden desire.
Low sub drop closes the curse quote. Under 120 Hz.
Drone returns for 'a curse is a law of nature'.
Soft timpani roll: nature's law, inevitable.
'उसे पूरा होना ही होता है': rising strings, then they melt into Brahmi's theme.
BRAHMI innocent theme, flute and harp, sweet. Her last happy moment.
Warm string pad, major colour.
Soft anklets as Brahmi approaches her father.
Reverse swell: something is wrong in the room. The warm pad starts to detune and sour.
Music drop-out one beat before 'बदल' (the gaze has changed).
Low brass stab plus sub: the changed gaze.
Tremolo plus contrabass, E / F cluster: a father's look turned dark.
BRAHMA corrupted: flat 6th held and out of tune, trombone underneath.
Sub drop into darkness ('अँधेरे').
Flight begins: fast staccato strings (low register, out of the voice pocket).
BRAHMI FEAR: the same falling shape, now fast violins. The audience recognises it.
Anklets hurry: she steps aside.
Head-sprout swell: rising organic whoosh with a wet crackle, no pitch.
Brass braam on 'उग' (the new head grows).
Run stops. 'अब सोचिए।' with only a held E tone.
Low brass pad rises slowly: the curse is stronger than a body.
Heartbeat returns, 72 bpm.
Short rise into beat 4 ('body began to change').
Rising ostinato: every escape direction pushes the pitch higher.
Head 3: taiko plus brass stab.
Head 4: stronger, a step higher.
She flies up: rising strings plus choir, high and thin.
Short music drop-out before 'पाँचवाँ'.
FIFTH HEAD BLOOMS: choir cluster, brass and timpani. Louder than heads 3 and 4 but not the series peak.
Five staring faces: choir cluster held, no pulse.
Braam on 'पाँच सिर।'.
SHRAAP, statement 3: 'one direction'.
The sons rush in: driven strings.
Two pairs of running feet (Marichi and Atri).
Plaintive shehnai line: the sons plead.
NARADA motif, bent and dark: the name that started it.
SHRAAP, statement 4: the curse beats the sons' words.
Words lose: music drop-out.
Defeat hit on 'हार'; its tail falls straight into the chase.
CHASE: taiko + dhol gallop, 132 bpm. Kept low and dry in the voice pocket.
Pursuit footsteps under the gallop.
BRAHMI FEAR, violins.
BRAHMA corrupted (trombone): 'that gaze followed her'.
Hundred forms: faster, 144 bpm, shape-shifting colour on top.
Shape-shift sparkle: the idea of changing form.
Cow: low horn with a slide, warm. Morph shimmer on 'बनीं' 122.52.
Bull: double taiko hit, heavy.
Mare: quick light flute run with hoof taps.
Stallion: low brass gallop answers the flute.
Duck: dry woodblock waddle.
Second duck: same figure a step lower.
Doe: light harp glissando up.
Stag: harp gliss plus a low horn note: end of the animal list, builds into the hundred.
The 'hundred forms' montage: fastest section, taiko / dhol roll, 168 bpm. Peak of the chase.
Insects: tiny fast pizzicato flurry.
Birds: high flute trill.
Animals: low horn call.
Air: gust.
Land: rushing hooves and stones.
River: splashing water.
Sea: big wave swell with a low gong, the whole list resolves into the ocean.
Relief: gallop drops out; light playful pizzicato for 'all animals of the earth' (an interesting fact). Lydian colour.
BRAHMI theme transformed into a bright, ringing harp phrase: her new name.
Harp glissando and glass shimmer on 'शतरूपा' (a hundred forms).
Low brass and sub rise quickly: Shiva is near.
Far thunder rolls: anger gathers.
Low brass swell on 'क्रोध से जलते'.
Drop-out one beat before 'शिव'. Total music silence, a held breath.
SHIVA ENTRANCE: taiko + sub + brass. First Shiva hit of the story.
Damaru roll: Shiva's own sound, tight and dry.
Close thunder crack on his arrival (above 5 kHz crack, sub tail).
SHIVA WRATH motif, horn + trombone.
Voice like thunder: low roll.
Brahma is shaken: hit plus glass crack.
Rage drops away; only a single held choir tone, 'होश लौटा' (sense returns).
Realisation: sombre strings.
BRAHMA motif pure again (the corrupted flat 6th is gone): the curse lifts, regret begins.
Cello pleading (same falling shape as Brahmi: the guilt and the victim share a tune).
Taiko march: Shiva's anger will not cool. Gets louder each bar.
Damaru roll resumes.
SHIVA WRATH, heavier, trombone + horn.
Brass, strings and taiko roll, steep rise on 'ब्रह्मा का पाँचवाँ सिर'.
Total music drop-out (about 0.5 s), one beat before the cut. No pause exists here, so only the voice is heard.

BIGGEST HIT OF THE EPISODE: the FIFTH HEAD cut. Taiko + timpani + brass braam + sub boom (below 120 Hz) + short high crack (above 5 kHz). Decisive; the tail carries under 'दिया।' and dies in the 0.12 s gap.
One close thunder-crack on the cut.
Large gong bloom underneath.
The head hits the ground: one heavy dull thud.
STILLNESS after the hit: only one long low E (contrabass + choir), no pulse. Shiva's verdict is spoken into hushed air.
Thin cold Kailash wind, after the storm of the hit.
Low male choir on a held fifth: the Vedas that will be chanted forever (no words).
BRAHMA motif, grand, peaceful: the four-faced Creator we know today. Closes part one's first act.
A single soft bell on 'चार'.
'पर कहानी यहीं ख़त्म नहीं हुई': unease creeps back, E / F tremolo.
Low brass stab: Shiva feels something.
Bone-on-skin sticky knock (same as the hook): the skull clings to his left hand.
He looks down. Only a held tone; the next two words are spoken into near silence.
BRAHMA hollow, lowest organ octave, with no choir.
SHOCK: skull clatter + low brass cluster on 'सिर'.
Straining, scraping low strings: he tries to pull it free.
'पर वह नहीं छूटा': braam on 'नहीं'.
Realisation dawns: a thin choir cluster.
'ब्राह्मण' low brass note.
Music drop-out before the heaviest word 'ब्रह्महत्या'. The gap after 'वध' is about 0.7 s.
BRAHMAHATYA: gong + brass braam + sub.
SHRAAP, lowest statement: the curse's price lands on Shiva.
Low sustain, with a far damaru pulse (soft) under 'सज़ा'. Unease, not shock.
Reasoning section: tanpura on Sa-Pa, calm and steady, the constant.
A single sitar pluck, rising and unresolved: the question.
Thoughtful pizzicato; 'फिर उन्हें सज़ा क्यों' leaves a suspended F chord hanging.
Pause 209.16-209.64: only the tanpura. The question is left hanging for a moment.
BRAHMI, a hint on cello: she asks too.
Atri's explanation: soft harp / sitar arpeggio, steady, logical, a calm answer.
One soft bell on 'फल' (fruit of action).
BRAHMA, gentle: 'our father also had to suffer'.
SHIVA WRATH motif, soft, weary and slow: 'so too Mahadev'.
Slow gentle crescendo: universal law applying to all.
Cadence: the lesson settles.
Bell closes the explanation.
KAPALI motif: low contrabass and cello, heavy, walking.
Lonely wind for the long wandering.
Slow solitary footsteps.
Bell 1 (pilgrimage): fails.
Bell 2 (penance): quieter, further away.
Bell 3 (mantra): almost gone. Hope fading in three steps.
'काम नहीं आया': only wind and footsteps; the lowest and emptiest music moment of this part.
Sorrow: slow bhairavi strings as the flesh decays.
Soft wet falling sounds, then dry bone.
A single bone clink.
Only the skeleton remains: music out, wind only.
KAPALI on solo cello with contrabass: slow and burdened.
The name KAPALI: low gong with a held cello-bass E. Weighty, sad, not violent.
Ages pass: soft reverse swell with a deep bell.
A first warm light: tanpura plus soft choir, hope.
Miracle: glass shimmer rises.
Soft swelling strings and choir toward release.
The skull finally falls: dull clatter on stone, with a long clear ring.
Stillness: only the skull's ring and the tanpura.
KASHI hint: bansuri turns the Kapali line upward. Release.
Conch on 'शुद्ध' (pure), distant.
Bright Yaman pad: awe at the sacred ground.
Temple bell: 'no ordinary ground'.
Warm strings crescendo (4 to 6): 'every person is freed from sins'.
KASHI, bansuri statement above the strings, sparse.
One larger temple bell on 'मुक्त' (freed).
Rise to the name of the city.
Short music drop-out before 'काशी'. Only the tanpura.
KASHI: choir bloom plus sub, the release of the whole first story. Tail (2.5 s) fades under 'इसी बीच' to nothing.
KASHI full statement on shehnai (with choir), the series' warmest sound.
Conch and temple bells on 'काशी'.
Brahmi's world: one tanpura on Sa-Pa, the only constant through her whole speech.
The Kashi glow cools: choir tail fades over 3 s.
Tender, close strings for the embrace ('सीने से लगाकर').
Pause 278.70-279.32 (0.62 s): strings stop, only the tanpura. A cello note breathes in at the end of the pause.
BRAHMI FEAR, solo cello, low and warm (below 250 Hz mostly), phrase 1 sits on 'डर लगता है'.
Cello phrase 2: starts a step higher, bends down at 'डर'.
Cello phrase 3: stretches over 'जब एक पिता... ख़तरा बन सकता है', a minor-2nd rub on 'ख़तरा' (287.34).
Very soft sul-tasto string harmonics, barely there; grow to 3.
Faint low E / F rub: the father as a danger. SHRAAP shadow, no motif, no horn.
'कौन करेगा?': cello leaps upward and stays hanging, joined by soft voice oohs. It does not resolve.
Pause 290.36-291.00 (0.64 s): only the held, unresolved cello tone and the tanpura. The question hangs unanswered.
'मनु चुप रहे': the held cello harmonic dies away. Silence is Manu's answer.
Pianissimo tremolo: 'काँपती रहीं', trembling.
Her speech, line 1: cello states the BRAHMI FEAR shape again, softly.
Violas and cellos, low and close, with the tanpura.
Slow harp arpeggio, like falling tears (sparse).
Line 2: BRAHMI FEAR a third higher on a solo violin, still quiet.
Strings thicken, violins join.
Line 3: choir oohs enter above the strings: a mother's grief becomes a chorus of every mother.
A very soft heartbeat enters under 'चुनाव देने से'; grows to 4 by line 4.
The cello answers the violin an octave apart: two voices of fear.
Line 4 ('ताक़त'): low horn pedal on E adds weight.
Rising tremolo strings: the voice starts to shake.
Slow, deep rise into the last line (thin above 4 kHz, deep under 200 Hz).
Soft timpani roll on 'कुचल न दे'.
LAST LINE, build: BRAHMI FEAR in full strings with choir, violins and cello, in unison over 'मुझे डर लगता है'. Voice pocket kept clear: celli below 250 Hz, violins above 2.5 kHz.
BIGGEST EMOTIONAL SWELL of the episode: full strings tutti, choir aahs, horn pedal and timpani, peak on 'मनु।'. The music breaks open on the name; fade tail runs over 'अब'.
Soft sub boom plus timpani under the swell. No crash cymbal, this is grief, not triumph.
The swell rings out and falls away under 'अब इसी कहानी का'. No gap exists, so the cross-fade into part 2 is on tanpura.
PART 2: key moves from E to G. Tanpura on Sa-Pa (G-D) is the constant.
Light glass sparkle: change of tone to a lighter story.
Playful pizzicato and glockenspiel (104 bpm): the tone becomes curious and almost comic.
Two water-drop tinkles on 'गिलास' and 'पानी' 320.28 (clear glass sounds).
NARADA motif, bright and bouncy (veena + glockenspiel), full statement.
NARADA, amazed: higher and quicker.
Mock-heroic horn fanfare on 'गर्व': Narada puffs up with pride.
Comic timpani pops on 'चार सिर!'.
Bigger pop and glock flourish on the second 'चार सिर'. Note: the joke is that he is proud of the curse.
Vaikuntha: luminous Yaman strings, tanpura continues, comic energy stops.
Soft conch on 'वैकुंठ'.
VISHNU motif, bansuri: a warm cradle shape.
VISHNU, again, with soft harp: his smile.
MAYA first glimpse: a shimmering santoor figure in the high register with a detuned pad underneath.
Pause 338.24-338.74: the shimmer rings alone.
NARADA, puzzled: a rising query that ends open. Covers the 0.42 s pause at 340.40.
Vishnu's line is gentle, the pad warm. Same pad will return at 407.16, so the audience hears the repeat.
One water-drop tinkle on 'पानी': the thirst that begins the illusion.
Soft bell: he leaves.
River water with birds (use the river ambience): the sound of the dream. Request: if there is no river bed, use soft flood sfx at intensity 1.
NARADA, strolling by the river.
Reverse swell: sudden stop.
He freezes: only the river and a single glass tone.
The detuned MAYA pad: the dream begins to wrap around him, slightly out of tune but beautiful.
Anklets of the maiden.
MAYA full: santoor shimmering above a glockenspiel.
Reverse glass bells: 'otherworldly'.
Memory dissolving into shimmer.
VISHNU motif played backwards and fading as he forgets Vishnu, the thirst and 'everything'.
MAYA wins: santoor takes over from the flute.
Gentle wedding shehnai (very soft).
Tinkling wedding bells.
A home on the sand: warm harp, tender and light.
Warm strings: domestic happiness.
River and birdsong continue gently, the sound of an ordinary happy day.
Dreamlike warm bed: slowly turning major chords, never repeating the same 8 bars exactly.
Harp glissando for 'साल आए, साल गए': time passes.
NARADA, slow and tender: father and grandfather.
Tinkle bells and celesta sparkle for children's laughter (no voices).
MAYA pad slips in underneath as attachment grows.
Single glass shimmer on 'मोह' (attachment).
Fullest and sweetest moment: 'पूरा संसार'.
NARADA, resolved on the tonic for once: complete peace, which is the trap.
Pause 377.48-378.08 (0.60 s): every instrument cut at once; only the river. The calm before the storm.
Wind rising: first sign.
Distant thunder: 'आसमान स्याह'.
Sub drone and tremolo (G / Ab) blot out the warm pad.
Music cut under 'बिजली', right before the crack.
LIGHTNING: close thunder crack with taiko and sub.
Storm: timpani roll building from 6 to 8 up to the sweep-away.
Heavy rain and rising river water, continuous, covers the whole flood.
Frantic strings and brass stabs (low, away from the voice pocket).
River swelling: surge.
Wave hit on 'लहरें'.
THE FLOOD SWEEPS THEM AWAY: brass braam + sub boom + wave crash, the loudest point of part 2 (below the fifth-head hit).
Big wave surge on 'बहा ले गईं'.
Three falling plucks on 'घर / आँगन / खिलौने' (each lower, each swallowed by water). Mirror of the later 'पत्नी / बच्चे / घर'.
Reverse and low-pass sweep downward: everything sinks.
Underwater muffled pad (low-passed), drifting: helpless.
Storm and music all cut on 'अचानक'; only a held tanpura. 'उन्होंने ख़ुद को पाया' is spoken in stillness. Rain tail must not run past 396.72.
Conch on 'वैकुंठ': clear sacred air after the storm.
Vaikuntha stillness: tanpura plus a soft Yaman pad.
VISHNU motif, calm and low.
Single bell on 'विष्णु के सामने' ringing across the pause 400.78-401.38.
Stillness in Vaikuntha: nearly nothing but tanpura and a very soft flute pad.
VISHNU, very low and slow.
A bell on 'पानी कहाँ है'.
Same flute pad and warm tone as at 340.82: Vishnu repeats himself, the loop closes.
He is stunned: all instruments out; only a single held glass tone.
Three single celesta notes, each lower, on 'पत्नी / बच्चे / घर'. The same falling figure as the toys sinking.
Pause 414.48-415.12 (0.64 s): total silence, a held breath before the realisation.
High, thin violins rising slowly: the sharp thought forms.
Arrow whoosh: fast, thin, dry.
Music out under 'चुभी' up to 'माया'; the word 'माया' will drop into silence. The 0.4 s of voice-free air after 'चुभी' is part of the pause.
MAYA REVEAL: soft sub boom, choir cluster, reverse glass swell. It blooms across the pause 418.64-419.36.
MAYA full statement: it now sounds terrifying and beautiful.
Glass shimmer cloud.
Detuned Maya pad under the explanation.
MAYA: 'एक विशाल भ्रम'.
'एक पूरी ज़िंदगी': slow glass ripples, life as a dream.
A tiny clock tick on 'बस उतना, जितना': so little time.
One water drop on 'पानी' (the glass of water that framed it). The other drop sounds from 319.84 and 342.44 return here.
Bell: the dream is done.
Wise and serene: tanpura on Sa-Pa for the entire teaching, with warm strings arriving and leaving.
VISHNU: he smiles, light and warm.
A small glass shimmer: Maya named.
Warm, steady strings under the explanation.
Falling harp arpeggio: a world that does not last.
BRAHMA, calm (the Maya link between the two stories).
BRAHMI FEAR quoted once, tenderly: the first story is the first example.
NARADA, slow and wistful: the second example is his own.
MAYA, gentle, with the detuned pad.
Infinite: a lingering high shimmer.
Slightly quickening harp: 'running after the perishable'.
ETERNAL: organ and choir on a bare open fifth (a return of the Parabrahman sound of episode 93). The one fixed point after all the illusion.
Soft deep gong on 'परब्रह्म'.
Sand slipping through fingers: falling harp.
Soft hiss of sand-like air.
Slow, gentle rise on 'माया से छूटता है'.
MOKSHA: soft sub bloom plus choir, calm, not heavy. The peak of the serene section.
Conch on 'मोक्ष'.
Temple bell.
Wide, calm pad: all of creation seen from above.
VISHNU motif over the world.
Light life ostinato: pizzicato for the living world.
Humans: a warm string touch.
Animals: a low horn touch.
Birds: a high flute touch.
Detuned MAYA pad creeping back, foreshadowing: everyone is about to cling to 'mine'.
Glass shimmer on 'अपना' (mine).
VISHNU, a knowing smile (one note slightly shadowed).
NARADA, left open (a question): 'be ready'.
Reverse swell with a low sub.
Soft braam plus sub on 'माया' (a warning, a promise).
MAYA, unresolved: ends on the 3rd, like a question.
Direct address to the audience: light, curious and warm; glock and pizzicato on tanpura.
NARADA, playful: 'put yourself in his place'.
Question shimmer.
MAYA on 'यह माया है?': the open question, ending unresolved.
A bright harp and glass sparkle on the call to action.
TEASER: the tone turns darker, 84 bpm. Slow build to the logo.
Gong on 'द्वार' (the gate).
SHRAAP, the main theme returns on 'श्राप': another curse is coming.
Taiko march begins on 'एक पिता'.
Braam on 'क्रोध'.
Rise into the last two words.
Final hit; a hard cut at 491.66 into the series logo. (Its tail must not run into the logo.)
SERIES LOGO (part 1/3): tanpura. Starts at the voice's end (491.66) and rings about 3 s past (needs a 3 s tail).
SERIES LOGO (part 2/3): conch.
SERIES LOGO (part 3/3): low boom.

requests: Logo/end tail: allow about 3 s of audio after the last voice sample (491.9 s to about 494.7 s) for c332-c334 (tail_s 3.0). If the video must stay 491.9 s, fade the logo out at 491.9 s.
Start logo: not placed because the voice starts at 0.14 s. Optional 1.5 s of pre-roll with tanpura, conch and low boom (then shift every cue by +1.5 s).

Sub boom, gong and thunder tails under speech (c04, c15, c95-c97, c110-c112, c203, c259) should be low-passed below about 120 Hz, with any crack above 5 kHz only; no energy in 250 Hz-4 kHz during the word.
The hit on 'काट' (c110, 168.88 s) happens while the owner is speaking, because no pause exists there: compress the voice-band only (duck 8 dB for 0.25 s, release 0.4 s), not the whole music bus.
